summary.headline: Sagar Cements guides FY27 volumes to about 7 million tonnes (FY26: 6.1 Mt) and Q4 EBITDA/tonne rose to ₹445 from ₹218.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 volumes grew 8% YoY and full-year volumes grew 11% to 6.1 million tonnes, with revenue up 20% in the quarter helped by non-trade pricing. Q4 EBITDA per tonne was ₹445 against ₹218 a year earlier, and quarterly PAT was ₹100 crore. Management flagged a fuel cost shock from the West Asia conflict (pet coke at $136-140 CIF versus about $120 earlier), with impact expected from mid-Q2 if prices do not ease. Management also announced a Superfine Building Materials division and in-principle approval for merging Andhra Cements into the parent.

segments.name: Plants (Q4 utilisation)
segments.commentary: Mattampally 59%, Gudipadu 84%, Bayyavaram 69%, Jeerabad 95%, Jajpur 44%, Dachepalli 38%. Jeerabad is cited as consistently running around 90%.

segments.name: Superfine Building Materials (new division)
segments.commentary: Approved by the board on 13 May 2026. It will use GGBS and fly ash to make superfine products (Blaine target 10,000-20,000) for UHPC, repairs and cladding. Management guides a minimum 30% margin; revenue and EBITDA numbers are deferred to next quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume target of about 7 million tonnes, relying on about 0.5 Mt from Jeerabad upgrade (expected by end-Q1), about 0.9 Mt from Andhra ramp-up and the balance from market growth of 12-15%.
FY27 EBITDA per tonne expected to be close to ₹600 if prices stay flat, with about ₹150/tonne from internal cost savings (WHRS, Andhra preheater, grinding units).

Pet coke and coal cost pressure: about ₹200/tonne at clinker and ₹100-150/tonne at cement on current blend, with impact from mid-Q2 if prices stay high. Management also pencilled in about ₹225-250/tonne in total fuel and miscellaneous cost increases, assumed to be passed through.
FY27 budget: ₹580 crore cost, about ₹100 crore lower than the prior year's cost base according to management's comments.

Capex: ₹190 crore pending on three ongoing projects (Andhra ₹140 crore, Gudipadu ₹17 crore, Jeerabad ₹33 crore). Maintenance capex about ₹50 crore per year. Some projects to be funded through lease or equipment finance.
Vizag land monetisation (about 100 acres, net about ₹3.5 crore per acre): ₹350 crore pencilled over 18-24 months, with ₹150 crore in year 1 after the government GO, and ₹150 crore assumed in FY27.
Net debt guidance for FY27 is to pay debt down from operating cash flow; year-end net debt was about ₹1,550 crore versus the earlier guidance of about ₹1,300 crore.
capex_capacity: WHRS: 2.8 MW of 4.35 MW (AQC boiler) commissioned on 12 May 2026; remaining 1.55 MW (preheater boiler) due by end-June 2026.
Jeerabad grinding expansion and Dachepalli expansion in progress; Jeerabad due before end of Q1 FY27.
Andhra Cements grinding expansion due by September 2026; new VRM for cement grinding due by September 2026.
Andhra clinker kcal consumption about 700 kcal/tonne of clinker versus about 775-780 earlier.
Madhya Pradesh incentives of about ₹171 crore over seven years; about ₹65 crore received so far, about ₹110 crore remaining over four years.
demand_pricing: Industry demand held up in the first two months of Q4 but slowed in late Q4 due to labour shortages, the festive season and unseasonal rains. Q4 volume growth was 8%, and Q1 FY27 to date is up about 7% YoY.
Price hike of about ₹25-30 per bag in second week of April (non-trade led) across regions; Hyderabad retail about ₹295 and wholesale about ₹268 after the hike.
Prices have been flat since mid-April, with some pressure in central and eastern markets (₹5 hike in Indore not sustained) and a slight negative bias there; south has held the April hike.
Demand outlook: AP and Telangana strong; Tamil Nadu 5-10%, Karnataka 5%, Odisha 5%, Madhya Pradesh 5-7.5%.
Management said bags cost fell about ₹2/bag, but the war impact on explosives and diesel (₹23.75/litre hike in commercial diesel) is expected to add about ₹100/tonne.
Superfine products priced around ₹30,000/tonne versus ₹2,500-3,000/tonne for low-Blaine GGBS, with low volumes expected initially.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected cost impact from the West Asia crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: Pet coke has risen from around $120 to $136-140 CIF, adding about ₹200/tonne at clinker and ₹100-150/tonne at cement. Inventory cover runs to mid-Q2, and imported coal is being partly switched to domestic coal, with the outcome known by end-Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise 28% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Around ₹11.5 crore was one-offs: about ₹7.5 crore mine bearing land (MBL) cess and about ₹3.24 crore DMF expense at a subsidiary, covering roughly 3-3.5 years of accrual. Promotional spend also rose. Excluding one-offs, growth is about 26%.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 volume of 7 Mt be achieved given past misses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target relies on Jeerabad (+0.5 Mt), Andhra ramp-up (+0.9 Mt) and market growth; it chooses not to chase share at the expense of cash.

qa_highlights.question: Will Jeerabad clinker sales continue in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Some clinker sales are expected during the phased ramp-up, subject to clinker prices, with margin held at that location's level.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any cost reduction left after Andhra stabilised?
qa_highlights.answer: Andhra clinker cost is now in line; the new VRM (by September) should deliver the planned savings. Margins are expected to be better in FY27 than FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net debt rise above guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoter unsecured debt for the Andhra project was drawn after the planned rights issue became an OFS, and solar capex was accelerated for short payback. Debt is expected to fall from operating cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital days rose sharply: why?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit days were extended in a difficult market, fuel prices were higher, and volumes grew. About ₹80 crore of US coal was bought in March on 180-day LC credit. Moderation is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Vizag land GO status and sale timing?
qa_highlights.answer: GVMC and UDA approvals are in place; the state GO is awaited, expected within six months. Management is assuming ₹350 crore over 18-24 months at the old reckoner rate of ₹4 crore per acre.

qa_highlights.question: Operating cost gap between standalone and Andhra?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gap is mainly logistics and market spread, with the Andhra cost gap closing after investments; detail to be discussed offline.

risks_watch: Fuel cost inflation: pet coke and coal may add ₹100-150/tonne at cement from mid-Q2 if prices do not ease; a ₹225-250/tonne total cost pass-through is assumed.
Pricing: the April hike is holding in the south, but central and eastern prices are flat to slightly negative.
Execution: Jeerabad upgrade (0.5 Mt), Andhra ramp-up (0.9 Mt), WHRS completion by end-June and VRM by September; past volume guidance has been missed.
Debt and working capital: year-end net debt about ₹1,550 crore, above prior guidance; working capital elevated; funding of ₹190 crore capex needs lease finance.
Vizag land monetisation depends on the state GO, which is still awaited; ₹150 crore is pencilled into FY27.
Incentive receipts: about ₹23 crore outstanding at March 2026, expected mid-July 2026.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume and margin recovery, with the Andhra turnaround and cost savings presented as key drivers. Cautious and somewhat evasive on fuel costs, the Superfine division financials and land sale timing, which management deferred to later updates.
key_quotes: We are more than hopeful to achieve 7 million tonnes for the current year.
We don't chase market share. We actually conserve the cash.
I think in the current year itself, we should be very close to ₹600 because the significant improvement for us has come from the cost itself

Andhra Cements grinding expansion and new VRM for cement grinding

growth.why: FY27 volume guided to about 7 Mt (about +15% vs 6.1 Mt FY26), backed by Jeerabad (~0.5 Mt, due end-Q1), Andhra ramp-up (~0.9 Mt) and 12-15% market growth, but the capacity additions have no hard date beyond end-Q1 and the 7 Mt target is partly reliant on market growth and pricing that management itself flagged as slowing.
